data.content_ref: inline:The argument assumes that 'high-variance' is synonymous with 'low-quality' or 'false,' yet in non-deterministic problem spaces (such as creative hypothesis generation or exploring novel mathematical proofs), high variance is often the primary source of valid, non-obvious solutions. By systematically filtering for 'coherence'—which often correlates with training data frequency and conventional wisdom—the harness may prematurely converge on local optima (plausible but incorrect answers) while rejecting the very divergent thoughts required to find the global optimum. A single model call, retaining its full entropy, has a non-zero probability of sampling these rare, high-value outliers which the harness's structural constraints would deterministically reject as 'noise.'
